differences.text: `menuContent` is `slot="menu"`, `children` the default slot, `triggerXstyle` is styling the host, `isDisabled` is `disabled`; the aliases `ContextMenuItem`, `ContextMenuDivider`, `ContextMenuCheckboxItem`, `ContextMenuRadioGroup`, `ContextMenuRadioItem`, `ContextMenuSubMenu` are the dropdown-menu tags (A§7.1). Added: `show()`, `showAt(x, y)`, `hide()`, `toggle()` and `requestClose()` (A§7.5).

The menu is anchored to a 0x0 viewport-fixed element at the pointer (the position controller's virtual anchor, A§9.10), so it uses CSS anchor positioning and the Floating UI module is never fetched in Chromium and Firefox. Upstream anchors to an element inside the trigger, so its menu follows the content when the page scrolls; here the menu stays at its viewport point while open.

Dismissal goes through the shared layer stack (Escape closes the top-most level once, IME composing Escape is ignored, outside presses close it) instead of upstream's own document listeners. ContextMenu and Shift+F10 are also handled on keydown so the menu opens at the focused element even where the engine does not synthesise a `contextmenu` event.

Touch long press uses Pointer Events (`pointerType === 'touch'`) instead of Touch Events: the same cancel rules plus `pointercancel` when the browser takes the gesture over. Mice and pens open through `contextmenu`.
The painted menu is the dropdown menu's Tecton surface (1px rule on the recessed popover fill, no drop shadow); part `menu` is the `astryx-context-menu` target.

core.context-menu.notes: Guides: [mwg:resilient-context-menus-and-nested-dropdowns] [mwg:accessibility] [mwg:accessible-web-components]. Compound content also renders in the bottom sheet (a `role=menu` container holding the slotted rows), as upstream.
